sections.section_title: Pathophysiology and Clinical Context of Abdominal Masses in Pregnancy
sections.description: Establishes the foundational medical knowledge required to understand the case, focusing on the epidemiology of uterine masses during gestation, physiological changes affecting diagnostic markers, and the safety of imaging modalities.
subtopics: Epidemiology and natural history of uterine leiomyomas during pregnancy
Physiological fluctuations of CA-125 levels across pregnancy trimesters
Safety profiles and diagnostic utility of ultrasound and non-contrast MRI in pregnancy
Pathophysiology of mass-related symptoms: mechanical compression and dyspnea

sections.section_title: Case Presentation and Multimodal Diagnostic Workup
sections.description: Details the specific clinical presentation of the patient, including physical examination findings, imaging results, and laboratory evaluations used to characterize the abdominal masses.
subtopics: Patient demographics, gestational age, and presenting symptoms (pain, dyspnea)
Physical examination findings: mass location, size, and tenderness
Ultrasound characteristics: cystic nature, vascularization, and adnexal involvement
MRI findings: wall thickness, fluid content, and relationship to uterine tissue
Laboratory evaluation: anemia, inflammatory markers, and tumor marker trends
Identification and management of concurrent Klebsiella pneumoniae infection

sections.description: Explains the clinical logic used to interpret diagnostic data, distinguishing between potential etiologies such as endometriomas, degenerating leiomyomas, and malignancy.
subtopics: Differentiating decidualised endometriomas from cystic degenerating leiomyomas
Interpreting elevated CA-125 in the context of benign pregnancy changes vs. pathology
Assessing risk factors for acute complications: torsion, rupture, and infection
Multidisciplinary risk assessment: balancing obstetric risks against surgical necessity
Role of imaging continuity in determining uterine origin of masses

sections.section_title: Surgical Management and Intraoperative Safety Strategies
sections.description: Covers the decision-making process for surgical intervention, the specific techniques employed during laparotomy, and protocols for ensuring fetal safety during the procedure.
subtopics: Indications for surgical intervention in the second trimester
Surgical approach: Rationale for laparotomy over laparoscopy in large masses
Intraoperative fetal monitoring and verification of cardiac activity
Selective myomectomy: Rationale for excising the upper mass and sparing the caudal mass
Pharmacological prophylaxis: Progesterone administration and antibiotic coverage
Management of surgical complications: Hemostasis and wound closure

sections.section_title: Obstetric Outcome, Delivery Planning, and Clinical Lessons
sections.description: Reviews the postoperative course, fetal development, decision-making regarding the mode of delivery, and summarizes key takeaways for future clinical practice.
subtopics: Postoperative management: Anemia correction and transfusion requirements
Obstetric follow-up: Fetal growth monitoring and amniotic fluid assessment
Decision-making for delivery mode: Elective caesarean section due to pelvic obstruction
Long-term maternal outcomes: Residual mass regression and symptom resolution
Clinical pearls: Guidelines for imaging, surgical timing, and delivery planning in complex cases
